line: Helen Zhou. I run the Saturday health talks here. Blood pressure checks, mostly. Then everyone asks about their cousin's prescriptions.
choice3: I'm not here for a checkup.

line: It is. But for some of them it's the only time they see a doctor all year. I've asked the clinic on Fifth to send someone. They keep saying they'll circle back.
choice1: Want me to ask them too?

line: I've been talking with Ruth Hale at the library about a joint forum. Some of our board think it's a waste of time. I think it's overdue.
choice1: Overdue. Put people in the same room.
choice2: Why do they think it's a waste?

line: You're the kind of person I wish sat on the parks committee. They meet Mondays. Nobody from this side of Grand has gone in years.
Ruth and I are finally doing it: a health and benefits fair at the library, Saturday. I want people from here walking in the front door. Will you help me bring them?
Three patients skipped follow-ups this week because the clinic asked for ID at the desk. One is diabetic. This is how policy shows up. In blood sugar.
The new rule means the clinic has to offer interpreters. Now I have to make sure people know they can ask. A rule nobody uses is just paper.
choice1: I can help spread the word.

line: You're here a lot. I'm glad. But don't let this be the only place you go. Mr. Guo would disagree with me there.
Ruth tells me you've become a regular at the library. Good. Bring some of that back here, would you?
Hello. I'm in the middle of something.
choice1: I owe you an apology for last time.
